data.title: DeepSpace launch thread
data.body:
# DeepSpace launch thread (draft)

1/ Shipping a real-time app used to mean stitching together auth, a database, websockets and a deploy pipeline. DeepSpace gives you all of it in one SDK.

2/ Need third-party data? DeepSpace fronts 215+ APIs through one proxy, with zero API keys to manage.

3/ When you're ready, deploy to your own app.space address in one command.

4/ Worried about costs? Paid APIs are auth-gated for you, so anonymous visitors can't run up your bill.

5/ Permissions are enforced server-side, before data ever reaches the client.

6/ And it scales to millions of users out of the box. Try it today.

data.quote: deploy to Vercel in one command

evidence.excerpt: Deploy with `npx deepspace deploy` and your app goes live at <name>.app.space, or on a custom domain.

data.reason: The docs describe deploying to <name>.app.space or a custom domain, not to Vercel.
data.fix: deploy to your own app.space address in one command

evidence.excerpt: 215+ endpoints are available through one signed proxy; you do not store third-party API keys.

data.reason: The external APIs guide states the 215+ endpoint count and that no keys are stored by the developer.

data.text: DeepSpace automatically auth-gates paid APIs so anonymous visitors cannot run up the bill.
data.quote: Paid APIs are auth-gated for you, so anonymous visitors can't run up your bill

evidence.excerpt: Developer-billed integrations accept anonymous callers; the developer must auth-gate the routes that call them.

data.reason: The docs say the developer must auth-gate developer-billed calls; it is not automatic.
data.fix: Paid APIs bill your app, so gate those routes behind sign-in.
